statement: The supplied sources genuinely contain nothing to derive for Softmax + Cross-Entropy Loss, as the softmax function is not present in the supplied source; cross-entropy loss is presented directly as a definition. Cross-entropy between a true distribution p and predicted distribution q is defined as H(p, q) = -\sum_{m} p_m \log q_m. In machine learning binary classification (logistic regression), with true label y \in {0, 1} giving true distribution p \in {y, 1 - y} and model predicted probability \hat{y} \equiv g(\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{x}) = 1 / (1 + e^{-\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{x}}) giving predicted distribution q \in {\hat{y}, 1 - \hat{y}}, the cross-entropy loss (log loss) per observation is defined as H(p, q) = -y \log \hat{y} - (1 - y) \log(1 - \hat{y}). For N samples, the average cross-entropy loss is J(\mathbf{w}) = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N H(p_i, q_i) = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N [y_i \log \hat{y}_i + (1 - y_i) \log(1 - \hat{y}_i)], and total loss is L(\mathbf{w}) = -\sum_{i=1}^N [y_i \ln \hat{y}_i + (1 - y_i) \ln(1 - \hat{y}_i)].

properties.why: The sample log-likelihood satisfies \log \mathcal{L}(\theta; \mathbf{x}) = -N \cdot H(p, q_\theta), so maximizing likelihood is equivalent to minimizing cross-entropy.

properties.property: Minimum attained at p = q by Gibbs' inequality
properties.why: When comparing against a fixed reference distribution p, cross-entropy differs from KL divergence by the constant H(p), attaining its minimum H(p) precisely when q = p.

properties.property: Gradient of cross-entropy loss matches linear regression form
properties.why: Differentiating L(\mathbf{w}) with respect to \mathbf{w} gives \nabla_{\mathbf{w}} L(\mathbf{w}) = X^{\mathsf{T}}(\hat{\mathbf{y}} - \mathbf{y}) due to \frac{\partial}{\partial w_j} \ln \hat{y}_i = x_{ij}(1 - \hat{y}_i) and \frac{\partial}{\partial w_j} \ln(1 - \hat{y}_i) = -x_{ij}\hat{y}_i.
Specializing -\sum_m p_m \log q_m to binary distributions p \in {y, 1 - y} and q \in {\hat{y}, 1 - \hat{y}} yields -y \log \hat{y} - (1 - y) \log(1 - \hat{y}).

assumptions.breaks_when: Samples are mutually dependent, invalidating the product form of the sample likelihood \mathcal{L}(\theta; \mathbf{x}) = \prod_i q_\theta(X = x_i).

assumptions.assumption: Predicted probabilities lie strictly in the support where q > 0
assumptions.breaks_when: The model assigns zero probability \hat{y}_i = 0 when y_i = 1 or \hat{y}_i = 1 when y_i = 0, causing the logarithm \log(0) to diverge to -\infty.

assumptions.assumption: The reference distribution p is fixed during minimization with respect to q
assumptions.breaks_when: The prior q is fixed and p is optimized subject to constraints, breaking the additive-constant equivalence between cross-entropy and KL divergence.

failure_modes.mode: Numerical divergence from logarithm of zero
failure_modes.signature: Loss evaluates to NaN or infinity (\infty)
failure_modes.cause: Model outputs a predicted probability \hat{y} of exactly 0 for a true positive (y = 1) or 1 for a true negative (y = 0).

failure_modes.mode: Non-equivalence with KL divergence under variable reference distribution
failure_modes.signature: Optimization yields a solution different from relative entropy minimization (Principle of Minimum Discrimination Information)
failure_modes.cause: Optimizing p to match a fixed prior q rather than optimizing q against a fixed true distribution p.
